headline: A Bloomberg Opinion column argues that DeepSeek and Huawei are eroding Nvidia's software advantage in China by making Huawei's AI chips easier to program.
score_reason: Opinion piece on a 30 Sep release; analysis is the new element, so lowered one point from 7.
importance_line: Chinese AI developers could find it cheaper to move off Nvidia chips if the free tools work well, which matters to Nvidia and Huawei and to US export-control policy, but the column is one writer's view and no performance results are given.
summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Catherine Thorbecke writes that DeepSeek has rebuilt its TileLang programming tools, a simpler alternative to the CUDA software that developers use to program Nvidia chips, for Huawei's Ascend AI chips and released them free, which could ease a switch away from American hardware. DeepSeek announced the release on 30 Sep 2026, as Reuters reported and The Next Web relayed; the column is an opinion, and it is not shown how well the tools perform.
notes: Read only the opening of the column (Business Times copy) because Bloomberg is blocked. Opinion, not reporting. Underlying DeepSeek release was 30 Sep 2026.
